Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:86: Now that we have spoken of the blemish in the covenant in general, and the punishment for emitting seed in vain, we must explain another matter that also blemishes the covenant — the sin of nocturnal emission [keri], for since it is an emission of seed in vain it is a blemish in the covenant. "Keri" is explained as "karya" — that the holy covenant is "cooled" [i.e., diverted] from its place, so that it bestows upon the external forces. In the Zohar (portion Pekudei, 264a), the second chamber of the chambers of impurity — this being the chamber where those who defile their covenant are punished — at the end of that chamber, Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains that there are two spirits there that transform into males and females, and these defile a person in a nighttime dream and cause him to emit seed in vain. And his punishment somewhat resembles the punishment for emitting seed in vain, for it says (Deuteronomy 23:10), "and you shall guard yourself from every evil thing [davar ra]" — meaning that he not fantasize by day and come to impurity by night (Avodah Zarah 20b), and we have already copied above their statement (Niddah 13b), that whoever brings himself to have a lustful fantasy is not admitted into the presence of the Holy One, blessed be He.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:87: Regarding the punishment of one who defiles himself, it is explained in the Zohar (portion Metzora, 55a), these are his words: Rabbi Elazar said, it is written (Leviticus 15:31), "and you shall separate the children of Israel from their impurity" etc., "lest they die in their impurity, by defiling My Tabernacle which is among them" — "and you shall separate" is like this [word] "zar" [stranger], who is a stranger to them all and does not join with what is not his own. Come and see: at the time people become impure below, they are made impure in everything, as has been said; but at the time the spirit of impurity is aroused, do not think it a "stranger" — rather, the spirit of impurity arouses another spirit of impurity, and permission is given to it to descend into the world. What permission? The permission that holiness had, which used to descend and strike within it, is not found and departs, and then judgment is revealed against the guilty ones, and judgment is added upon judgment, and then two spirits are found in the world — a spirit of judgment and a spirit of impurity.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:88: Rabbi Elazar said, I must say here a matter I learned from my father: come and see, we learn this from the affliction of a house — for when an impure spirit dwells in a house, and the Holy One, blessed be He, wishes to purify it, He sends the affliction of tzara'at into the house so that they contend with one another, and that affliction does not depart from the house — even though the impure spirit has departed from that house — until the house is demolished, its stones and wood and everything, and then that place is purified. Likewise, whoever becomes impure and arouses an impure spirit that rests upon him — when the Holy One, blessed be He, wishes to purify the world, He arouses a spirit of harsh judgment, which is found in the world and rests upon that impure spirit, and they contend with one another until it is removed from the world; and that spirit of harsh judgment does not depart from its place until it demolishes the place, the limbs and bones and everything — then the world is purified and the impure spirits are removed from it, and the world is found in purity. Therefore we have learned: whoever comes to be defiled, is certainly made impure — woe to himself when an impure spirit rests upon him and is found in him in the world, for certainly we should know that the Holy One, blessed be He, wishes to eliminate him from the world. Fortunate are the righteous, all of whom are holy, and are found in holiness before the Holy King, upon whom a holy spirit rests, in this world and in the World to Come. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:89: From this statement it likewise appears that a penitent must perform great mortification for the sin of nocturnal emission until he purifies himself from the impurity — for "keri" leads to impurity, and judgment must rest upon him until he is purified, as explained in the statement, if it is not corrected by repentance in the manner explained in Tikkunim, in the statement we copied, saying, "and bear several sufferings to remove that serpent from there," and as my teacher, peace be upon him, explained, which we copied above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:90: Now, keri comes from several causes, and we must explain them. The first of them is what Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in portion Kedoshim (84a) regarding "do not turn to idols" (Leviticus 19:4) — this refers to the matter of gazing at women, from which one comes to fantasy and impurity, and he transgresses "and molten gods you shall not make for yourselves" — since his whole body becomes heated with the spirit of impurity, he makes himself a molten god, and the word "for yourselves" is explained as though it said, "do not make yourselves molten gods," along these lines. And likewise it is explained in the Zohar (portion Tetzaveh, 182b) regarding "you shall not make molten gods for yourself" (Exodus 34:17), regarding anger — that anger differs from all other impurities. These are his words: but this differs from all, and the whole body becomes impure within and without, and the soul and everything becomes impure. And he says below, therefore it is written, "you shall not make molten gods for yourself" — "for yourself," in order to harm yourself.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:91: Along these lines it says in the Zohar (portion Kedoshim, there): and whoever gazes at a woman's beauty by day comes to fantasize about it by night, and if that evil fantasy rises upon him, he transgresses "molten gods you shall not make for yourselves." Thus far his words. The meaning of "if that evil fantasy rises upon him" is that he was drawn by the fantasy until, through it, he comes to impurity — he is like one who worships idols, as explained at the beginning of the chapter.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:92: Also, one must be careful not to engage in excessive conversation with any woman, especially with his wife when she is a niddah, along the lines of what is said in the first chapter of Avot (1:5), "do not engage in excessive conversation with a woman" — with his own wife they said this, all the more so with another's wife; from here the Sages said, whenever a person engages in excessive conversation with a woman, he causes evil to himself. The meaning of "causes evil to himself" is that he draws Lilith, who is called "evil," and she defiles him with a nocturnal emission. And likewise it is explained in the Zohar (portion Vayishlach, 169b) on the verse (Psalms 91:10), "no evil shall befall you, nor shall a plague come near your tent" — for when a person walks in a straight path and conducts himself in holiness, "evil," which is Lilith, and "plague," which are the afflictions of people, do not come near him; but if, God forbid, he does not walk in a straight path, they defile him. Along these lines we interpret "causes evil to himself" — that he draws upon himself the evil Lilith, to cause him to sin. Therefore, in the end, he descends to Gehinnom, to consume that evil which has attached to him. And he becomes idle from words of Torah — before they abolished the requirement of immersion for one who had a nocturnal emission, he was forbidden words of Torah, and this too was an ordinance of Ezra; and even today some are strict not to occupy themselves with Torah while impure [in this way].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:93: Speaking with one's wife while she is a niddah is explained in Midrash Bamidbar Rabbah, portion Nazir (10:8), these are his words: why did the Torah forbid the pressings of grapes, from which one does not become intoxicated, and also forbid the eating of everything that comes from the vine, things from which one does not become intoxicated? Why so? From here we learn that a person must distance himself from what is disgraceful and from what resembles the disgraceful — from here we learn that the Torah made a fence for its own words. There we have learned (Avot 1:1), "be deliberate in judgment, raise up many disciples, and make a fence for the Torah." How does one make a fence for one's own words? In the manner that the Torah made a fence for its own words — behold, it says (Leviticus 18:19), "and you shall not approach a woman in her menstrual impurity to uncover her nakedness." One might think he may embrace her and kiss her and speak idle words with her — the verse teaches, "do not approach." [One might think] he may sleep with her in her clothing — the verse teaches, "do not approach." One might think she may wash her face and paint her eyes and he may take the cup from her — the verse teaches (ibid. 15:33), "and she who is ill in her menstrual impurity" — all the days she is ill she shall be in a state of banishment [from these]. From here they said: whoever makes herself unattractive in the days of her niddah, the spirit of the Sages is pleased with her; and whoever adorns herself in the days of her niddah, the spirit of the Sages is not pleased with her.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:94: Behold, it says (Leviticus 18:6), "none of you shall approach any close relative to uncover nakedness." From here they said, a person should not be secluded with women in a single inn, even with his sister, and even with his daughter and mother-in-law, because of the accusations of people — here it says "do not approach," and there it says "do not approach" [of the niddah] — regarding whatever leads to a matter of transgression, "do not approach": distance yourself from the disgraceful and from what resembles the disgraceful. So the Sages said: distance yourself from a light sin lest it lead you to a severe one; run to a light mitzvah, for it will bring you to a weighty one. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:95: Regarding what is called excessive conversation with a woman, they were strict in tractate Eruvin, these are their words: Rabbi Yosi HaGelili was walking on the road and met Bruriah. He said to her, "by which way shall we go to Lod?" She said to him, "foolish Galilean, did not the Sages say, do not engage in excessive conversation with a woman? You should have said, 'which way to Lod?'" Thus far their words. From here the God-fearing person should learn to minimize speech with a woman as much as possible, and especially with his wife when she is a niddah, as explained in the statement. And I found written, "*I was mute, *I was silent, *I held my peace" (Psalms 39:3) — the initial letters spell "niddah," to indicate that one must especially minimize speech with her.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:96: And just as one must be careful not to engage in excessive conversation, so one must be careful not to touch her, and the other details of the laws that Rabbi Yosef Karo wrote in the Tur, Yoreh De'ah, and likewise not to gaze at her; for by transgressing any one of these he draws upon himself the power of impurity that is in his wife, and it is possible they will defile him. This warning we learn from Rashbi, peace be upon him (Zohar, portion Bereshit, 20), these are his words: in like manner, one whose wife is in her days of impurity and guards her properly — all those days the supernal union is found with him and male and female are found [united above]. Thus far his words — and from the affirmative you infer the negative: that if he does not guard her properly, the Shechinah departs from him. And you already know that the external forces are called "these" [eleh], for they are ready to rest immediately upon a person, as explained in portion Vayechi (Zohar, 228a), and it is possible they will defile him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:97: Especially in a place where there was holiness and the holiness has departed, there they run to attach themselves — the proof of this is at a person's death, as explained in the Zohar (there, portion Vayechi, 226a), that because holiness had rested there, they want to attach themselves there. For this reason my teacher, peace be upon him, used to say that any person who conducts himself with abstinence and purity, and afterward departs from that holiness, it is possible they will defile him, for the reason mentioned — that they pursue a place where there had been holiness. And I add a further point: the kelipot are called vanity and emptiness, and they pursue only something that is empty like themselves; and once they find a vessel that has been emptied of holiness, they attach themselves to it — especially given what is explained in the Zohar (portion Mishpatim, end of 111), that all their desire is after the thigh, and all the more so the thigh of Torah scholars; therefore Torah scholars need especially to be warned, since these run to attach themselves to them, and whatever aspect they find to attach to, they immediately attach themselves and defile them. Of this it is said (Psalms 89:31-33), "if his children forsake My Torah and do not walk in My judgments, if they profane My statutes and do not keep My commandments, then I will visit their transgression with the rod and their iniquity with plagues [nega'im]." And "plagues" are the afflictions of people that come from nocturnal emissions — it is thus explicit that once holiness departs, one is immediately visited with these sufferings.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:98: The reason that the visitation for emitting seed in vain is through the covenant is that the supernal covenant encompasses Torah and the commandments, in the secret of "Yours, O LORD, is the greatness" — "kol" [all] in heaven and earth (1 Chronicles 29:11), translated as "that grasps heaven and earth." Thus, in blemishing Torah by not occupying himself with it properly, or [blemishing] the commandments, he has profaned the holy supernal covenant, and therefore he is visited with impurity of his covenant.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:99: This matter is alluded to in the Zohar (portion Vayishlach, end of 176), these are his words, regarding "more than all the powders of the merchant" (Song of Songs 3:6): another interpretation, this is Joseph the righteous, etc. Another interpretation: why "merchant" [rochel]? Just as a shopkeeper has all the packets of spices and powders of the perfumers in his hand, so too Joseph is the fulfillment [kiyum] of Torah, since he maintained it — for all the commandments of Torah are bound up with the guarding of the holy covenant. Thus far his words. And likewise it says in the Zohar (portion Miketz, beginning of 197): therefore Joseph, who guarded the covenant, merited the supernal kingship and the lower kingship, and therefore whoever guards the holy covenant is as though he fulfills the whole holy Torah, since the covenant is equivalent to the whole Torah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:100: It is necessary to say the reason explained — that it is the secret of "kol" [encompassing all] — for otherwise, if a person kept the covenant but did not recite the Shema and did not lay tefillin etc., would it be considered as though he had fulfilled all the commandments? Surely not! Rather, certainly it is as explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:101: Also, the essential root cause of nocturnal emission is because of the sin of the covenant of the tongue, as explained above (ch. 11) regarding (Psalms 34:14), "guard your tongue from evil." Also, one who reveals [Torah secrets] to one who is unworthy — his punishment is nocturnal emission. The reason is that the receptacle for the supernal secrets flowing from Tzadik, called "yod," is "the secret of the LORD is for those who fear Him" — those who are in the Shechinah — this is the secret of "the LORD is [close] to those who fear Him." And when one is unworthy, he draws the light of Torah from within but finds no vessel in which it can rest, and it goes out in vain to the external forces — he is found threshing within and winnowing without, and this is the sin of Er and Onan; therefore, measure for measure, his seed will be poured out in vain and they will defile him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:102: Also, one who recites blessings in vain is like one who emits seed in vain, and it is possible they will defile him; one must be careful about this, especially the prayer leader, who should not repeat the Amidah if there are not certainly nine who will answer Amen.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:103: Also, another cause of nocturnal emission is the pleasure of sleeping all night, as explained above in chapter 5, and this is included in "if his children forsake My Torah." The reason for this is that since he becomes lax from occupation with Torah, the Holy One, blessed be He, becomes his enemy, as it is written (Proverbs 24:10), "if you falter in a day of trouble, your strength is small" — and this is measure for measure: he did not wish to attach himself to a God-fearing woman [i.e., the Shechinah] through occupation with Torah, so he attaches himself to the externality of a strange woman, and begets a demon to accuse him, and "he shall eat of the fruit of his ways" — for no evil descends from above; rather, since a person attaches himself to the Other Side, holiness departs from him, and then the external forces, who are ready, rule over him, and he is called "eleh" [these/no-god], as it is said (Deuteronomy 31:17), "because my God is not within me, these evils have found me." Therefore, upon waking from his sleep, he should hasten to rise; for if he does not rise but returns to sleep, he might sleep on his back, facing upward, which is cursed by the mouth of the scribes, as we say (Berachot 13b): Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi cursed one who lies on his back.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:104: Also, the cause of keri is explained in the Torah in what is said (Leviticus 26:21), "and if you walk with Me in keri and do not wish to listen to Me" etc., and it is written (ibid. 26:28), "and I will walk with you in the wrath of keri" etc. Rashi, peace be upon him, explained: our Sages said, "keri" means occasional, that it is only occasional [not consistent] — so you will walk occasionally in My commandments. And Menachem explained it as a term of withholding, as in (Proverbs 25:17), "withhold [hoker] your foot from your neighbor's house," and (ibid. 17:27), "a man of understanding is of a cool spirit [yekar ruach]." This term is close to Onkelos's translation, "kashyu," hardness — that they harden their hearts to refrain from drawing near to Me. Thus far his words, and the two interpretations converge on a single intent.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:105: Behold, what is written after it: "and I too will walk with you in the wrath of keri." Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, portion Terumah, 130a), these are his words: "in the wrath of keri" — in that anger that issues from the opening of keri, and these are those who roam about at night, and at the time souls go out to ascend to appear above, these go out and accuse them so they cannot ascend, except those holy, pious, supernal ones who split the firmaments and the airs and ascend. And these groups of pure ones go out and inform people of false matters, and appear to them in various forms, and mock them, until they emit their seed — and they are called the "masters of keri," since it is those who issue from the opening of keri who cause them [these emissions]. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:106: Therefore it is fitting for a person to be established and faithful in divine service, like a pillar that does not waver from it; and likewise the word "brit" [covenant] means establishment, as in (Genesis 31:44), "come, let us make a covenant, I and you." Therefore one who wishes to merit the attribute of Tzadik must be faithful and strong in service; of this it is said (Ecclesiastes 8:5), "one who keeps the commandment shall know no evil thing." And you already know what was explained above regarding "evil" [rah].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:107: Likewise, if one breaches any of the fences set up by our Sages, it is possible they will defile him — for the fences our Sages of blessed memory set up were so as not to give the external force a place to enter within, into holiness, and if one breaches a fence, a snake will bite him, since through the breach he has given it a place to enter. This is likewise explained in Tikkunim (18b): the sea is Torah, and "sand" toward the sea is like a chain for a dog — one who releases the chain causes the dog to bite him, and this alludes to the fences our Sages of blessed memory set up. These are his words there: "and the children of Israel shall keep the Sabbath" (Exodus 31:16) — this is the only daughter, who is a safeguard for Israel every single Sabbath, and whoever profanes it is not guarded by the Holy One, blessed be He; moreover, it is said of it, "whoever profanes it shall surely die" — whoever brings into her domain a maidservant, a profaned woman, or a harlot — for her domain is the Sabbath boundary [techum Shabbat], like the boundary and border of the sea, of which it is said (Jeremiah 5:22), "I have placed the sand as a boundary for the sea" — and what is this? (Hosea 2:1), "and the number of the children of Israel shall be like the sand of the sea" — and there is no sea but Torah; whoever transgresses it is as though he returns the world to chaos and void, and Shabbat is equivalent to the whole Torah — whoever transgresses it is as though he returns the world to chaos and void, and therefore the verse is adjacent to it: "and the earth was chaos and void" — for it [the sand] is like the sand toward the sea, like the link of a chain for a dog: whoever removes it from its chain causes several bites of suffering to bite him. Because of this David said (Psalms 22:21), "deliver my soul from the sword, my precious life from the power of the dog" — this is Samael, who is held by a chain-collar; on Shabbat he is held by the collar. Thus far his words. It is thus explicit that the Sabbath boundary and the sand toward the sea are both a single matter, to distance Samael and keep him away from holiness, and whoever breaches the fence causes Samael to bite him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:108: Likewise, among the things one must be careful about so as not to be defiled, is that if he makes a vow, he should fulfill his vows for the service of the Name, as it is said (Psalms 15:4), "he swears to his own detriment and does not retract." If he does not fulfill the mitzvah and breaks his vow, it is possible he will become impure, as it is written (Ecclesiastes 5:5), "do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin." This verse is explained in the Midrash as referring to vows, as we copied their words above in chapter 14; see there. Along these lines, "and destroy the work of your hands" refers to the covenant, as is explained in portion Bereshit (8a) and we copied his words in chapter 11.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:109: The reason is that the verse says (Numbers 30:3), "according to all that proceeds from his mouth he shall do" — the reason being, as we have already explained, that speech is spiritual, resembling physical seed; and just as from the lower covenant one must not emit seed in vain except into a female, so one must not emit speech in vain except by bringing it to the place of action, which is the female. We find in this that the voice that issues unites the covenant of the tongue with the female; and if, God forbid, he did not fulfill [his vow], he has thereby emitted seed in vain — namely, the voice and speech that issue from the covenant of the tongue — and therefore he will also blemish the covenant of the body through emitting seed in vain, for one sin drags another after it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:110: The remedy for the sin of nocturnal emission: first, he must immerse in a mikveh of forty se'ah, in order to purify himself from the accursed external impurity, and even one who is lenient about immersion for the purpose of marital union should not be lenient about this one. Rashbi, peace be upon him, likewise explained this (Zohar, portion Bereshit, 55a): and since one who has had a nocturnal emission comes from the side of the impure spirit, he must wash from himself and purify himself from it, as the fellowship have established. Thus far his words — and before this, the matter of Na'amah, mother of the demons, is discussed, who defiles all those who cause people to have nocturnal emissions.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:111: If forty se'ah is not possible, he should strive to have nine kav poured upon him. And if even this is not possible for him, at the very least he should wash the soiled place; and in the book Ma'aseh HaChasidim (Sefer Chasidim §157) it is written that one should not think words of Torah until he has rubbed his thighs with water — so it is fitting to do for the honor of Torah and prayer.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:112: In portion Metzora, in the portion of the zav, they brought in the Yalkut, in Tana d'Bei Eliyahu, these are his words: a man had a nocturnal emission and was liable for immersion; he said, "who sees me? there is no harm in this," and dismissed it from his mind. Again he had a nocturnal emission and said, "who sees me?" etc. — three times; he thereby transgressed what is written (Job 33:29), "twice, three times, with a man" — for he becomes a zav from the beginning of his ways, as it is said (Leviticus 15:2), "any man who has a discharge" — why does it say "any man" [ish ish, doubled]? To include a nocturnal chance emission. If he repents and returns, he is healed; if not, he remains in this state until the day of his death, as it is said (Leviticus 15:3), "and this shall be his impurity in his discharge." Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:113: Regarding the merits of immersion, we have already written above in its place (Gate of Love, ch. 11), and we said that one of its special properties is to return the soul to its place, for one who is impure has no soul [in a sense], and one who blemishes the covenant has his soul depart from him. This is likewise explained in the Zohar (portion Lech Lecha, 94a), these are his words: for we have learned, whenever a person is marked with this holy sign of this letter, he actually beholds the Holy One, blessed be He, from it, and a holy soul attaches itself to him; if he does not merit to guard this sign, what is written? (Job 4:9), "by the breath of God they perish" — for the mark of the Holy One, blessed be He, was not guarded. And if he merits to guard it, the Shechinah does not separate from him — when is it established in him? When he marries and this sign enters into its place. Thus far his words. See further there to understand the matter in its full form; to avoid excessive length, we have not copied all his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:114: Incidentally, we learn from this statement a remedy for the sign of the covenant: that he strive to marry in his youth, in order to purify himself. For this reason they said in Kiddushin (29b): Rav Chisda said, the reason I am superior to my colleagues is that I married at sixteen; and had I married at fourteen, I would have said to Satan, "an arrow in your eye." Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:115: In Tikkunim (82b) it says: further, "a fruit tree" (Genesis 1:11) — this is the middle pillar; "bearing fruit" — this is Tzadik; "whose seed is in it upon the earth" — this is the Shechinah, in whom all seeds are included. And here is the commandment of procreation, to produce fruits and seeds, of which it is said (Isaiah 45:18), "He did not create it a waste, He formed it to be inhabited"; and whoever refrains from procreation is as though he returns this earth to being desolate, and withholds blessings from it, each according to his level — whoever blemishes below blemishes above, in the place from which his soul was hewn. Thus far his words. And if one has blemished and cannot correct himself at the proper time, if God grants him a son he should endeavor to marry him off before he comes to sin. And in this generation a person must keep his son away and guard him from everything that might lead to sinful fantasy before he marries.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:116: Further, the remedy for the sign of the covenant is also through occupation with Torah, as explained above in the statement we copied from Tikkunim (66b), and it is explained in Tikkunim (98b) that whoever has blemished the soul, his correction is through occupation with Torah in the six orders of the Mishnah. These are his words: moreover, whoever brings his seed into a niddah, a maidservant, a Cutheite woman, or a harlot, is as though he mixes together what the Holy One, blessed be He, separated, as it is written (Genesis 1:6), "and it separated between water and water" — namely, the waters of a niddah and the pure waters — this being forbidden and that permitted, this fit and that unfit, this impure and that pure. These are the six orders [of Mishnah] through which Mishnah [teaching/repetition] was given, to distinguish between good and evil, which Adam and the generations after him mixed together. Thus far his words. See further in Tikkun 46.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:117: And if he strives to know the six orders of Mishnah by heart, how good and pleasant is his portion — for the essence of Mishnah is to know it by heart, as it is said (Exodus 34:27), "for according to these words [al pi, literally 'by the mouth of'] I have made a covenant with you" — and matters of the Oral Torah you may not put in writing (cf. Gittin 60b), and they were written down only because of "it is a time to act for the LORD" (Psalms 119:126); and fortunate is one who knows them by heart, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains in the second chamber (Zohar, portion Bereshit, 42a). He says there that in the chamber of the substance of the heavens are Seraphim with six wings, and afterward says: these are they who burn up those who do not care for the honor of their Master, and the secret of one who makes improper use of the crown perishes — whoever reads and repeats the six orders of Mishnah is one who knows how to arrange and bind the unification of his Master properly. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:118: The essential knowledge of Mishnah is to strive to know it with its explanation, and whoever reads it with its explanation will not quickly forget it, as is said in the Yerushalmi (Berachot 5:1): Rabbi Tanchum said, whoever understands what he studies does not quickly forget it. And along these lines, knowledge of Torah by heart is in the attribute of the male, since all remembrance is in the male; and since this sin [of keri] blemishes the sign of the covenant, which is in the place of the male, and descends into the place of forgetting, it is fitting that it be corrected through remembrance, by knowing Torah by heart.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:119: Likewise, Torah is a remedy so that one not come to nocturnal emission, and this matter is alluded to in the Zohar (portion Vayeshev, 190a), these are his words: Rabbi Elazar said, when that evil side comes to entice a person, he should draw him toward Torah, and it will separate from him. Come and see, for we have learned that when this evil side stands before the Holy One, blessed be He, to lead the world astray because of evil deeds, the Holy One, blessed be He, has compassion on the world and gives people counsel to be saved from it, so that it not prevail over them nor over their deeds. What is this counsel? To occupy oneself with Torah and be saved from it. From where do we learn this? As it is written (Proverbs 6:23), "for the commandment is a lamp and the Torah is light, and reproofs of discipline are the way of life" — what is written after it? "To guard you from an evil woman, from the smooth tongue of a foreign woman." This is the impure side, the Other Side, which continually stands before the Holy One, blessed be He, to lead people astray because of their sins. Thus far his words, as relevant to our purpose. Now it is known that all the powers of keri come from a "strange woman," as they explained in the Zohar: it is written, "for the commandment is a lamp and the Torah is light" etc. "to guard you" — thus Torah is a guard, protecting a person from these powers.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:120: Especially one who is unmarried should never lie down in bed to sleep until he is satisfied with Torah, as we say in Berachot (14a): Rabbi Yochanan said, whoever satisfies himself with words of Torah and goes to sleep is not brought bad news, as it is said (Proverbs 19:23), "and satisfied, he shall lodge without being visited by evil." Thus far his words. And it is already known that "evil" [rah] refers to one who emits seed in vain, as in (Deuteronomy 23:10), "and you shall guard yourself from every evil thing," which our Sages of blessed memory explained (Avodah Zarah 20b) as meaning that one should not fantasize by day, etc. Therefore it is fitting not to lie down until he has read much Torah, in such a way that he is satisfied — for just as a person satisfies himself from eating, he should satisfy himself with Torah until he tires so that he cannot study further, like a person satisfied from abundant eating who cannot eat more.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:121: Nevertheless, if he occupied himself with Torah during the day and is satisfied from it, he is not obligated to prolong his occupation with Torah at the beginning of the night in such a way that he cannot rise at the night-watch. The wise man's eyes are in his head, and he manages his affairs with judgment: he should occupy himself with Torah during the day until he is satisfied, and at the beginning of the night he should also occupy himself with Torah, so that the soul rise through the breath of Torah, but not to the point of satiation, so as not to be prevented from rising at the night-watch, which is the essence of the occupation with Torah, as it is said (Lamentations 2:19), "arise, cry out in the night," as explained above (ch. 7).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:122: Further, the remedy for the sign of the covenant is to be careful in all the qualities by which a person is called righteous [tzadik], which depend on the supernal attribute of Tzadik. One of them is that he strive to rise at midnight, or from midnight onward, to occupy himself with Torah, and strive to join night to day through Torah, corresponding to what separated them — for one who rises at midnight is called righteous, as explained in portion Emor (90a), which we copied above (ch. 7); and it is explained there that "He gives prey to those who fear Him" (Psalms 111:5) is said of those who occupy themselves with Torah from midnight onward, the reason being that they join with the attribute of fear/awe.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:123: And likewise it is explained in the Zohar (portion Miketz, 194b) that the verse "the LORD favors those who fear Him, those who wait for His kindness" (Psalms 147:11) is said of those who rise from midnight onward and bind night to day in order to receive the thread of kindness. These are his words: "those who wait for His kindness" — say, these are they who occupy themselves with Torah at night and join with the Shechinah, and when morning comes they wait for His kindness, etc.; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:124: Regarding the merit of one who binds night to day through occupation with Torah, the verse explains, saying (Psalms 33:18), "behold, the eye of the LORD is toward those who fear Him, toward those who wait for His kindness, to deliver their soul from death and to keep them alive in famine" — and "the eye of the LORD" is explained in the Idra (Naso, 129b) as the open eye of Arich [Anpin], etc.; see there. And certainly one who does this corrects the attribute of Tzadik with the Shechinah, drawing for himself and for her the thread of kindness, as explained in several places. And corresponding to what he separated from the Shechinah by drawing the drop outward — the secret of the drop being white, drawn from the right side, as explained in Tikkunim (41a) regarding "and the manna was like coriander seed" (Numbers 11:7) — corresponding to this he binds night to day to receive the thread of kindness. And likewise it is explained in the Zohar (portion Vayigash, 207b) on the verse (Psalms 88:2), "O LORD, God of my salvation, by day I cry out, at night before You" — that one who rises at midnight and occupies himself with Torah stands at the level of the "righteous, life of the worlds" [Tzadik, Chai Olamim], and then during the day he merits the thread of kindness, and this is what is meant by "God of my salvation," since the thread of kindness is salvation, as it says (Psalms 60:7), "save with Your right hand" — we shall not copy his words in full, to avoid excessive length.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:125: Further, one must be careful to unite with his wife only from Sabbath to Sabbath, on Rosh Chodesh, and on festivals, since there is no union above through Tzadik except at these times, as it is written (cf. Ezekiel 46:1), "the gate that faces east shall be closed the six working days, but on the Sabbath day it shall be opened, and on the day of the new moon it shall be opened." This is likewise explained in the Zohar (portion Noach, beginning of 75b), these are his words on this verse: this verse must be examined, for it contains a secret in what is said, "it shall be closed the six working days, but on the Sabbath day it shall be opened, and on the day of the new moon it shall be opened." Why should it be closed all those six working days? Rather, these are the weekdays, on which this gate is closed so that the weekday not make use of the holy. "But on the Sabbath day it shall be opened, and on the day of the new moon it shall be opened" — for then there is a use of holy for holy, and then the moon is illuminated to join with the sun. Thus far his words, as relevant to our purpose.
